newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: MANILA'S PROPERTY SHARES SUB-INDEX FALLS 4.11 PCT.
newsitem.headline: MANILA'S PROPERTY SHARES SUB-INDEX FALLS 4.11 PCT.

text.p: The Philippine property shares sub-index dropped 54.75 points, or 4.11 percent, to 1,278.18 points in late trade on Monday on concerns over high interest rates, brokers said.

"It's still the same story. Interest rates are still high and the investors are still worrying about their effect on the bottomline of companies," said Cilette Liboro, research head at Orion-Squire Capital.
Ayala Land Inc was leading the losers in the property sector, shedding 1.25 peso, or 5.95 percent, to 19.75 pesos.
The property sub-index's fall was the steepest among the stock market's six indices late in the session.

"The sentiment is still bad as long as interest rates are at these levels. It's bad for corporate earnings and for property issues which are very sensitive to interest rate fluctuations," said Ramon Saulo, acting research head at Asiamerit Securities Inc.
The central bank has been cutting its overnight rates since it raised it to a 2 1/2 year-high on July 10 to defend the peso.
But they still remain relatively high.
